items.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) has significantly advanced autonomous GUI agents. However, during the development of GUI agents for dynamic scenarios, error compounding leads to a labor-intensive and expensive bottleneck, requiring high costs for manual intervention. Meanwhile, errors are hard to be located and difficult to track failure reasoning. Consequently, it is challenging to overcome random errors simply by blindly increasing the size of the training dataset and address errors in a targeted manner. Existing research primarily attempt to improve GUI agent by optimizing the agent&apos;s internal design to avoid outcome deviation, ignoring the critical need for automated self-correction in step-level agent errors. In view of this, we propose the Automated Oversight (AO), an efficient four-stage closed-loop approach designed to emulate human-level oversight. The architecture consists of four key phases: (1) global outcome verification for final-state checking; (2) step-level visual trajectory alignment to intercept errors in real-time; (3) teacher-driven root-cause diagnosis to analyze failures; and (4) closed-loop rectification with state rollback to recover the task. Unlike traditional methods, AO focuses on failure-aware reasoning to identify the root causes of errors and execute targeted recovery. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can improve agent success rates and reduce human cognitive burden by achieving reliable autonomous interactions in dynamic systems. We will publicly release our code.</jats:p>
title: Automated Oversight Diagnostic Self-Correction and Failure-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents(ChinaMM)

items.abstract: <jats:p>Grounding natural language queries in graphical user interfaces (GUIs) poses unique challenges due to the diversity of visual elements, spatial clutter, and the ambiguity of language. In this paper, we introduce DiMo-GUI, a training-free framework for GUI grounding that leverages two core strategies: dynamic visual grounding and modality-aware optimization. Instead of treating the GUI as a monolithic image, our method splits the input into textual elements and iconic elements, allowing the model to reason over each modality independently using general-purpose visionlanguage models. When predictions are ambiguous or incorrect, DiMo-GUI dynamically focuses attention by generating candidate focal regions centered on the model's initial predictions and incrementally zooms into subregions to refine the grounding result. This hierarchical refinement process helps disambiguate visually crowded layouts without the need for additional training or annotations. We evaluate our approach on standard GUI grounding benchmarks and demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline inference pipelines, highlighting the effectiveness of combining modality separation with region-focused reasoning.</jats:p>
title: DiMo-GUI: Advancing Test-time Scaling in GUI Grounding via Modality-Aware Visual Reasoning
